questions.explanation: After a negative adverb at the start, invert the auxiliary and subject.

questions.q: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the documents.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' at the start triggers inversion.
A fronted negative adverb needs subject-auxiliary inversion.

options: Never I have been so embarrassed.
Never had I be so embarrassed.
Never have I been so embarrassed.
Never have been I so embarrassed.
questions.explanation: After 'never', the auxiliary comes before the subject.

questions.q: Hardly ___ the phone when it rang again.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' with a past event uses inversion with 'had'.

questions.q: No sooner ___ the door than the phone rang.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than' and needs inversion.

options: Not only she won, but she broke the record too.
Not only did she won, but she broke the record too.
Not only won she, but she broke the record too.
Not only did she win, but she broke the record too.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' at the start inverts 'did' and the subject.
'Seldom' at the start triggers inversion.
'Little' meaning 'not' at the start needs inversion.

options: Hardly we had started when it began to rain.
Hardly had we start when it began to rain.
Hardly had we started when it began to rain.
Hardly did we had started when it began to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' pairs with 'when' and inverts 'had' and the subject.
'Only then' at the start triggers inversion.
A fronted negative place adverb inverts the auxiliary and subject.

options: No sooner he had arrived than he was asked to leave.
No sooner had he arrived when he was asked to leave.
No sooner did he arrived than he was asked to leave.
No sooner had he arrived than he was asked to leave.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' needs inversion and pairs with 'than'.

questions.q: Never before ___ such a large crowd.
questions.explanation: 'Never before' at the start inverts 'had' and the subject.
'Only by...' at the start triggers inversion.

options: Seldom do we see such dedication.
Seldom we do see such dedication.
Seldom does we see such dedication.
questions.explanation: 'Seldom' at the start inverts 'do' and the subject.
'Under no circumstances' triggers inversion with the modal first.
'Not until' at the start needs inversion.

options: Little did she know what was waiting for her.
Little she did know what was waiting for her.
Little knew she what was waiting for her.
Little did she knew what was waiting for her.
questions.explanation: 'Little' at the start inverts 'did' and the subject.

questions.q: So tired ___ that he fell asleep instantly.
questions.explanation: 'So + adjective' at the start triggers inversion.
